The least unrestricted total is a lower bound for the box optimum. A gauge-optimal row fits the box whenever its total is at most the least capacity. The actually added masses w_z−d_z give a feasible correction and ensure positive retained mass.

The feasible optimal removal row has raw moment r*j+b. The prescribed nonzero continuous normal on the retained side is realized by choosing its opposite for removal. Each full-dimensional measured fiber has a null cutting boundary, so taking the closed complement gives exact optimum and integer base j. Positive retained mass gives a point in its strict halfspace and hence ambient interior by density of interior points.

The capacities stay bounded below and b=t b₁+o(t), so continuity and positive homogeneity give the expansion. For A>0, the normalized addition mean lies in Q; a boundary supporting functional achieves equality only if every positive growth site lies in that exposed face. Rank zero gives strict gain for positive addition.
